channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Thailand Puts 49 Data Centers on Hold Over Resource Strain
item.description: Thailand’s embrace of data centers hit a speed bump after the government suspended construction of 49 server farms as public concerns about the power-hungry facilities’ impact on communities intensify.
item.dc:creator: Anuchit Nguyen

item.title: Korea’s Memory Chip Lead Over China Set to Grow, Report Says
item.description: South Korea’s lead over China in memory chip production is expected to widen further thanks to an aggressive expansion of domestic facilities by Samsung Electronics Co. and SK Hynix Inc., according to the Bank of Korea.
item.dc:creator: Yoolim Lee

item.title: Anthropic Finalizing $15 Billion Pre-IPO Credit Facility
item.description: Anthropic PBC is set to finalize an expansion of its revolving credit facility to $15 billion, according to people familiar with the matter, ahead of the firm's public filing for its initial public offering. The maker of the Claude chatbot is seeking to raise as much as SpaceX or more in the IPO, people familiar with the preparations said. Morgan Stanley is leading the process, the people said. Bloomberg's Anthony Stephens reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Oura CMO on Ring-Maker's Demographic Appeal, Cost
item.description: Oura's Chief Medical Officer Dr Ricky Bloomfield says their ring will help detect diseases, as the company files for an initial public offering, showing soaring revenue as well as increasing losses. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Novo Owner to Build $62 Million Quantum Chip Plant in Denmark
item.description: The foundation that controls Ozempic maker Novo Nordisk A/S is building a new quantum chip factory in Copenhagen as the global race to develop the emerging technology heats up.
item.dc:creator: Sanne Wass

item.title: India Launches Rocket in Boost to Space Ambitions
item.description: India’s space program notched a much-needed success with a rocket launch on Friday, after two consecutive failures of another launcher that had long served as its workhorse rocket. Bloomberg's Mihir Mishra reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Andreessen-Backed AI Startup Gimlet Is Valued at $3 Billion in New Round
item.description: The company, which helps divide AI tasks among different chips, raised $300 million in its latest round
item.dc:creator: Dina Bass

item.title: SoftBank’s ¥1 Trillion Retail Bond Rejuvenates Japan Debt Market
item.description: SoftBank Group Corp. priced a ¥1 trillion ($6.3 billion) retail bond in an offering that expands Japan’s retail corporate debt market and gives investors a viable alternative to bank deposits and stocks.
item.dc:creator: Takahiko Hyuga

item.title: Magnetar Founder on AI’s Impact on Investors’ Mindsets
item.description: Alec Litowitz, Founder of Magnetar and now head of his family office, Qstar Capital, discusses his new book, "The Adaptability Quotient," which focuses on decision-making when old strategies stop working. He links the book’s themes to his experience at Magnetar, saying the firm looked for periods of rapid change because uncertainty often drives others away and creates opportunity for those first able to resolve it. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Skylar CIO: AI & Power Story Will Play Out Over Years
item.description: Bill Perkins discusses a new ETF built around short-dated electricity futures in PJM and ERCOT, saying it gives investors direct exposure to power pricing rather than to utilities themselves. He argues the product is timely because electricity demand is expected to grow, driven by manufacturing reshoring, data centers, and the broader AI buildout. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Crusoe Raises Over $3 Billion in Funding at $30 Billion Valuation
item.description: Crusoe, a cloud-computing provider and data center developer doing business with OpenAI, Microsoft Corp. and Meta Platforms Inc., has raised over $3 billion in a funding round that values the startup at roughly $30 billion, according to people familiar with the situation.
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Torrence, Dina Bass and Edward Ludlow

item.title: ValueEdge Chair: SpaceX Needs A Succession Plan
item.description: Nell Minow, Chair of ValueEdge Advisors, says Anthropic is moving in the opposite direction from SpaceX on governance, but argues its structure is still unusual and potentially problematic. She says the company is combining elements of public companies and nonprofits, including a public benefit corporation framework that she says both cares about shareholder value and does not. She speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Apple Headhunter on Ternus Era: Best AI Talent Will Win
item.description: Jeff Christian, who says he oversaw the last two board searches at Apple under Steve Jobs and argues that the selection of John Ternus signals a strategic shift. The discussion then moves to what a hardware engineer can bring to Apple, especially given concerns that the company’s bigger challenges may lie in software and AI rather than hardware. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: David Booth: Shocked People are Anxious About Investing
item.description: David Booth, Co-Founder of Dimensional Fund Advisors, discusses his new book, "Stay Calm," which blends memoir and investment guidance. Booth’s discusses his long-standing message to investors: ignore short-term market noise, avoid trying to outguess the market, and stay invested rather than panic during volatility. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: India Space Surveillance Gets Boost With GSLV Launch Success
item.description: India’s space program notched a successful rocket launch on Friday, placing an Earth-observation craft into orbit as New Delhi works to sharpen its satellite-based surveillance capabilities.
item.dc:creator: Mihir Mishra

item.title: FBI Investigating Possible Exposure of Millions of American IDs
item.description: The FBI is investigating a potential breach of an ID verification company that may have exposed scans of millions of Americans’ driver’s licenses, a bureau spokesperson told Bloomberg News on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Patrick Howell O'Neill

item.title: Los Angeles Schools Ban Student Use of AI Tools on District Devices
item.description: The Los Angeles Unified School District is barring students from using generative AI tools on district devices as part of a broader push to reduce screen time in the classroom.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Oxford and Erin Hudson

item.title: Adobe Names Chakravarthy CEO, While Other Contender Departs
item.description: Adobe Inc. named Anil Chakravarthy, the leader of its marketing and analytics software business, as its next chief executive officer, thrusting the company veteran into a challenging competition with artificial intelligence upstarts.
item.dc:creator: Brody Ford

item.title: Crusoe Signs Roughly $13 Billion AI Cloud Deal With Jane Street
item.description: Crusoe, a data center upstart with contracts to supply AI computing power to the likes of Meta Platforms Inc. and Oracle Corp., has signed a cloud contract with trading firm Jane Street Group valued at around $13 billion, according to people with knowledge of the matter.
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Torrence and Dina Bass

item.title: Chipmaker Longsys Said to Raise $903 Million in HK Listing
item.description: Shenzhen Longsys Electronics Co. has raised HK$7.08 billion ($903 million) after pricing its Hong Kong listing below the maximum, according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Julia Fioretti and Sangmi Cha
